correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation gives \(\dot J=-(\sigma+1)J\) exactly. Backward exponential growth rules out nonzero \(J\) on bounded complete trajectories. On \(J=0\), uniqueness fixes the common complex phase and reduces every nontrivial bounded complete orbit to the displayed three-dimensional real system. Along a recurrent non-equilibrium orbit, the imaginary variational block has one zero phase exponent and constant trace \(-\sigma-1\), hence its other exponent is \(-\sigma-1\). The real base block has one zero flow exponent and constant divergence \(-\sigma-1-\beta\), so its remaining pair sums to that negative number. The bundled exact checker verifies all polynomial identities and divergence/trace calculations.

No located source states or implies this theorem. The closest indexed result is an analogous phase-locking theorem for the complex Rikitake dynamo, but it concerns a different vector field and gives a different normal rate and quotient system.
residual_risks: The 2008 and 2021 full texts were not both lawfully accessible during this check; an unindexed equivalent phase reduction in inaccessible material remains possible.

value.rationale: The same-system literature explicitly analyzes Lyapunov exponents and even labels parameter regimes hyperchaotic. The exact phase-locking identity shows that all compact recurrent integer-order dynamics collapse to fixed-phase three-dimensional leaves and that any non-equilibrium compact ergodic state has at most one positive asymptotic exponent. This is a structural correction to how recurrent complexity in the five-dimensional representation can be interpreted, not a routine parameter substitution or numerical recomputation.
